findings.title: Restarting a 'hung' process can run two flushers on the same shards, producing duplicate segments
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a process is deemed hung (`cause == "hang"`), `process.kill()` is called and a replacement is immediately spawned via `_create_process_for_shards`. `kill()` is asynchronous — the old process can still be inside its flush loop while the new process starts flushing the same shards. Both processes can call `buffer.flush_segments()` and produce the same segments to Kafka before either calls `done_flush_segments`, resulting in duplicate segments in the buffered-segments topic (duplicate span data downstream). The old process is also never joined, so it is never confirmed dead before the replacement starts. The replacement should only be started after the old process has actually exited (join with timeout), and ideally after verifying no in-flight flush.

findings.title: Thread-based flusher (produce_to_pipe path) is never killed on restart, so restarts stack threads
findings.body: When `produce_to_pipe` is set, the flusher 'process' is a `threading.Thread`. On an unhealthy restart, the kill is guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so the old thread is left running and a new one is spawned for the same shards. A hung thread never recovers, so every restart adds another thread; if the hang is caused by a stuck `produce` (as in the backpressure test, where append sleeps), multiple threads will flush the same shards concurrently, duplicating messages. This mostly affects the test path today, but the code claims Thread support, so it should either kill/stop the old thread cooperatively (e.g. per-process stop flag) or refuse to restart thread-based flushers.

findings.title: Metric tag key inconsistency: 'shards' vs 'shard'
findings.body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`. The tag name typo means the wait_produce timer cannot be grouped/joined with the other flusher metrics by shard, and produces a second tag key in the metrics namespace for the same dimension.

findings.title: Restart counter never resets, so cumulative restarts eventually crash the consumer even if each process is healthy
findings.body: `process_restarts[process_index]` is only ever incremented; there is no reset after a process proves itself healthy. With MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS = 10, a shard-group that legitimately restarts 11 times over the entire lifetime of a long-running consumer (e.g. due to transient Redis/Kafka failures hours apart) will trigger `RuntimeError` and crash the whole consumer, taking down all shard flushers. The counter should reset (or decay) after a period of healthy operation, as was the case before this change for the single process — but this PR now makes it much more likely since a single misbehaving shard-group among many takes the consumer down.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code
findings.body: The method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is never called anywhere (the restart path calls `_create_process_for_shards` with a process index directly). It also has a bug if it were used: it would overwrite `self.processes[process_index]` without killing the previous process. It should be removed.

findings.title: No test that multiple flusher processes actually flush their shards end-to-end
findings.body: The new `test_flusher_processes_limit` test only asserts process/shard bookkeeping (counts and map sizes); it never submits a span or asserts that a segment is produced. There is no test covering the core new behavior: that with multiple flusher processes, spans on shards assigned to different processes are all flushed exactly once, nor a test for the restart path (`_ensure_processes_alive` with multiple processes), which is where the trickiest new logic lives. A regression in shard-to-process mapping or in restart handling would pass the current test suite.

findings.title: submit() iterates self.buffers while restarts mutate it
findings.body: `submit()` and `_ensure_processes_alive()` run on the main thread, so the dict mutation itself is not racy in-process. However `_create_process_for_shards` replaces `self.buffers[process_index]` with a brand new `SpansBuffer(shards)` each restart. If a restart happens between the `record_stored_segments()` loop and the memory-info loop within a single `submit()` call, some shards' buffers get recorded twice and some not at all within that call; more importantly each restart allocates a new SpansBuffer (with new Redis clients) while old ones are never closed, leaking Redis connections over repeated restarts.
